THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
CHAIR'S STATEMENT AND STRATEGIC REPORT
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2025
- 1 -
The directors present the strategic report for the year ended 30 September 2025.
Overview
Financial Year 2024-2025 was a period of continued scale, R&D acceleration, and strategic positioning for Informed Group. Building on foundational investment, the business has continued to successfully pursue a dynamic innovation path, making operational and commercial foundations more resilient and ensuring stability, productivity, profitability, and sustained growth throughout the period.
Our operating model – blending high-performing in-house talent with a robust B2B partner ecosystem has proven both scalable and resilient, enabling sustained growth despite a challenging political and economic backdrop, exacerbated by geopolitical instability.
Financial highlights include maintaining record revenue achieved over the 2023-2024 period alongside sustained gross margins, driven by a 20% increase in staff headcount. The addition and mobilisation of several high-profile, long-term contracts, alongside successful diversification and growth in volume of Informed’s client base, have secured a healthy forward delivery pipeline for the 2025-2026 period.
Operationally, the business has increased delivery capacity and capability to meet the continued demand from national-scale customers. Informed’s headcount increase has been realised through the continuing success of the business’s graduate recruitment programme, alongside the addition of high-quality, experienced professionals, which have ensured both the successful 100% retention of clients and significant client estate growth through the effective onboarding of a significant number of new nationally significant customers operating in both Public and Private Sector markets.
Significant positive cash flow has been used to increase investment in workspace for the business’s growing employee base, as well as to fund a dynamic research and development programme that has resulted in new Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced data science intellectual property assets and capabilities, which continue to accelerate domestic and international growth.
Increased investment in product and service diversification has strengthened both the profile and uptake of InformedDECISION™, a first-of-its-kind Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) platform that allows organisations to make better, faster, more informed decisions.
Alongside this, InformedINSIGHT™, an open-standards-based data integration and analytics platform that enables organisations to turn data science into real-world decision support, was funded through a Civtech Innovation challenge and was rolled out nationally for operational use by the Scottish Government.
Following the change of Government in mid-2024, the business successfully navigated the slowdown in public sector procurement in the first two quarters by strengthening its focus on private-sector business development with strong customer growth in the transport sector. Through the second half, the business added significant public sector clients from central Government and Environment and Land Management, pharmaceutical and healthcare, and a growing base of regulators operating across policing and healthcare.
The business continues to view the global digital skills shortage as an opportunity to invest in domestic and international skills development through our world-class ISO-accredited InformedACADEMY™ learning and development framework. This framework has been extended to include artificial intelligence and data science modules, which are increasingly attractive in domestic and international markets. InformedACADEMY™ has been further expanded to present our people, clients, and partners with accelerated career development and commercial growth opportunities.
The business has continued to focus on an enhanced people engagement strategy, which has seen us recognised as a certified GREAT Place to Work® for a fifth year running, with employees giving an average recommendation rating of 85% across 22 key workplace criteria.
International trade and market development are central to Informed’s growth ambitions. The business has invested in recruiting in-country leadership in Malaysia alongside an International Engagement Lead based in the UK. Informed has grown and strengthened its alliance partner ecosystem and network of associates and subcontractors, enabling commercial activities to support domestic and international growth through the 2025-2026 period and beyond.
THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
CHAIR'S STATEMENT AND STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2025
- 2 -
Overview - continued
Based on the business’s proven ability to deliver high-impact, trust-based innovation for critical national infrastructure, Informed was invited to participate in the UK-Ukraine Tech Bridge, supported by the Department for Business and Trade. This programme has led to engagement with European partners and prospects, with growth prospects for the 2025-2026 period.
Our Business Progress
The business invested in acquiring and developing market-leading skills and capabilities in data science, service design, and delivery management disciplines. Over the 2024-2025 period, we have continued to prioritise skills development in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), geospatial and location intelligence, DevOps, DevSecOps, MLOps, WebOps, and Continuous integration methods, all of which are in increasing demand from existing and potential clients both in domestic and international markets.
The business has continued to invest in significant internal improvement initiatives, further enhancing productivity and business success. Continued cloud modernisation, enhancements to client and partner relationship management, and improvements to live service operations have strengthened our infrastructure and ability to scale. Enhanced bid quality assurance, alongside strengthened client and prospect engagement management programmes, has enabled the business to achieve an 84% pitch-win ratio over the period.
The business successfully diversified and grew its client estate: Informed’s teams, supported by a growing partner ecosystem, continue to deliver high-impact, trust-based innovation and digital transformation platforms and services for clients across the healthcare and pharmaceutical, civil defence, sustainable environmental management, transport, and central government sectors, with significant growth in the regulator market. Notable client wins have included the Medicines and Healthcare Regulatory Authority (MHRA), The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), His Majesty’s Inspectorate for Constabularies and Fire and Rescue Services (HMICFRS), The Department for Business and Trade, The Department for the Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA), and The Manchester Airport Group.
Continued investment in AI-based products and platforms has seen increased use and advancement of InformedDECISION™, a first-of-its-kind AI-powered digital land asset management and planning platform, and InformedINSIGHT™, an open-standards-based data integration and analytics platform. Both platforms have been successfully rolled out by the Scottish Government for operational use to protect and promote environmental and land resilience, and to revolutionise planning.
InformedDECISION™ functionality for the healthcare market has resulted in additional product licensing revenues for the 2024-2025 period, based on an innovative revenue-sharing model, with further growth anticipated in 2025-2026.
Launched in January 2025, Informed’s AI Readiness Assessment service and model continue to generate organic and new business growth for public and private sector clients, with Thompson Hospital Group in Malaysia, HMICFRS, NICE, and MHRA all identifying proofs of value for significant AI adoption across operational efficiency and service delivery.
The process of obtaining ISO 42001 certification for responsible management and the application of AI began in Q4 of the 2024-2025 period. At the time of writing, Informed Solutions is proud to announce it has attained ISO/IEC 42001 certification, the world’s pioneering international standard for Artificial Intelligence Management Systems (AIMS). Achieving this certification is a key milestone and fulfils a commitment in our AI Charter, which sets the ground rules we follow with our clients, partners, and teams to realise the benefits of AI in an ethical, safe, and responsible way. This success will effectively position Informed as one of the World’s few certified and trusted AI partners in the 2025-2026 period.
Internationally, Informed’s teams extended and strengthened valued relationships with DBT, FCDO, MyDigital Corporation, The National Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) body, the Malaysian Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), and Austrade colleagues through market engagement initiatives in target ASEAN markets (Malaysia and Australia). Additionally, our collaborative relationship with the Department of Business and Trade has led to Informed being welcomed into the UK-Ukraine Tech Bridge, an initiative designed to help rebuild Ukraine following the conflict with Russia.
THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
CHAIR'S STATEMENT AND STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2025
- 3 -
Market Presence
Continued investment in Informed groups’ engagement and business development capacity and capability has strengthened outreach and engagement with key industry partners and government stakeholders in the UK, Malaysia, Australia, and Europe.
Sponsorship of significant events with Industry bodies, including techUK, Digital Leaders, ScotlandIS, ASEAN and Australian business and international chambers, Several Department for Business and Trade International Trade Weeks, and London Tech Week, on key data science, data analytics and AI topics has continued at pace and scale, increasing the business’s profile at the heart of important digital industry, innovation, and economic growth debates.
Evidence of Informed groups' industry leadership has accelerated over the period, with the expertise and influence of Board Directors increasingly recognised and rewarded. Elizabeth Vega OBE was appointed Chair for the UK’s largest tech representative body, Digital Leaders. Additionally, she represented industry on the Department for Business and Trade Small Business Council and continued her leadership of the Cabinet Office Small and Medium Business Panel and stewardship of the Cabinet Office Procurement Advisory Panel in support of seminal procurement reforms, which resulted in Prompt Payment regulation in 2025. In September 2025, Elizabeth was invited to join Minister Richard Lockhead’s Scottish Government Technology Council.
Seth Finegan, UK CEO, was appointed Deputy Chair of techUK’s prestigious Public Sector Board, Transformation Director, Justin Hassall was elected to techUK’s Health Council, and the group's Main and Technical Board Directors continued to develop dynamic and visible leadership roles in digital sector engagement activity through our formal industry stakeholder partnerships and conference programmes. Informed continues to place emphasis on participation and leadership recognition of its extended future leaders cohort.
Informed retained its certification as a Great Place to Work® for a fifth successive year with an average rating of 85%. Great Place to Work® certification, providing independent recognition and proof that Informed's values and support for its people are industry-leading.
Market Landscape
Looking ahead, the UK economic outlook appears more stable than in the previous period, with inflation gradually easing and modest growth expected; however, growth is likely to stay uneven, with business investment and confidence under sustained pressure and ongoing sensitivity to global uncertainty and domestic policy changes. Projected public sector cost reductions have continued throughout the period in efforts to balance the debt-to-GDP ratio.
Despite these challenges, innovation in data science and novel digital technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), remain highly attractive propositions for Informed's core markets, including healthcare, civil defence, energy transition, environmental management and transport.
There is also a potential for rightsizing in the AI market. Despite massive investment and hype, many AI companies and related investments are currently operating at a loss or experiencing significant volatility. Informed Group’s continued advancement in high-impact, trust-based innovation has strengthened the group’s position and offerings for both public- and private-sector clients. The business’s continued ability to prove value through responsible, ethical applications of data analytics and AI is well placed to strengthen Informed’s growth prospects over the 2025-2026 period.
Significantly increased business development activity in private-sector markets and the opening-up of public-sector spending mean that Informed will enter the 2025-2026 period with a healthy pipeline of business, reinforced by a continued, award-winning track record of excellence in innovation, performance, and delivery.
Continued investment in Informed’s products and platforms is accelerating Informed's domestic and international growth, with a significant senior Malaysian Director appointment, leading dynamic market development activity across the ASEAN region.
A phased investment approach to product and market diversification will ensure sustainable growth through 2025-2026.
THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
CHAIR'S STATEMENT AND STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2025
- 4 -
Research and Development
Informed maintained its long-term outlook, investing heavily in research and development (R&D) to accelerate and de-risk large-scale digital change initiatives.
Both InformedDECISION™ and InformedINSIGHT™ commercial-grade platforms are rolled out for full operational use across Scotland, with a significant number of land management and planning organisations across the UK and internationally becoming interested in and attracted to trusted, proven capabilities. R&D efforts for both platforms continue to focus on developing wider markets, including healthcare, civil defence, transport, and infrastructure.
Informed’s proven expertise in identifying service-centric AI proofs-of-value (PoVs) that operationalise AI in complex environments to swiftly and effectively deliver tangible business value has been productised into a Five-stage AI Readiness Assessment. This provides a structured, evidence-based assessment of the value of AI to an organisation and its publics, including current readiness, and the people, technical, and data capabilities they need to unlock value at pace and scale.
This approach combines data science, User-Centred Design, and agile delivery to ensure PoVs can rapidly scale into enterprise / national applications. Importantly, our approach combines assessment with upskilling, the development of practical roadmaps and target operating models for safe, trustworthy, ethical and responsible AI. The assessment is already being adopted by a growing number of clients and prospects. ISO42001 certification for Responsible Management of AI will strengthen this offering over the period.
Growth in Talent and Capacity
The technical and digital skills shortage remains a challenge for all businesses. Informed's response to this has included adding leadership to our talent attraction team and increasing our market presence through events, recruitment fairs, and community sponsorships. 2024-2025 was another successful year for graduate and experienced professional intake, resulting in a 20% increase in permanent staff headcount, further extending our capacity to deliver client services at scale and pace.
Improving our People Strategy has provided our staff with even greater clarity about their development and careers, resulting in industry-leading retention rates of +85%. Our Learning and Development team continues to execute a strategy that allows our people to fully engage in shaping our approach to attracting, developing, and retaining great colleagues and talent in the Group, and a clear set of principles to guide the development and evolution of everyone at Informed.
Investment in digitising skills and learning and development has seen a new Learning Management System rolled out to all Informed teams across all offices, with employees and partners now able to take advantage of InformedACADEMY™, our ISO9001-accredited learning and development framework.
As with previous periods, Informed's ongoing commitment to improving diversity and inclusion within the digital and tech sector remains as strong as ever. The DNA of our business and workplace culture is built on the principles of fair, equal, and respectful treatment of our people, all areas where we scored over 94% in our Great Place to Work® certification in 2025.
THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
CHAIR'S STATEMENT AND STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2025
- 5 -
Our Commitment to Social Value
Informed strives to deliver meaningful and measurable social value through its people, partner, and purpose-led innovation. A continued commitment to operating as a responsible, inclusive, and sustainable business has been embedded into a social value programme that not only meets Informed’s vision and mission as a purpose-led organisation but meets public and private sector client requirements as advised in the Social Value Model.
Our Social Value Programme is structured around  four key pillars , which together reflect our holistic approach to delivering long-term, sustainable impact. Each pillar is explored in detail throughout this report, demonstrating how our actions create measurable value for people, society, and the planet:
Supporting Healthy and Inclusive Communities  – promoting wellbeing, mental health, equality, and inclusion through internal initiatives and external partnerships.
Skills for Growth and Sustainability in the Workforce  – investing in people, ensuring lifelong learning, and addressing national skills shortages in high-growth technology and data sectors.
Responsible Business and Resilient Supply Chains  – championing ethical practices, fair work, and local economic growth through purpose-driven, fair procurement and supplier engagement.
Environmental Stewardship and Sustainability  – leading by example in reducing our environmental impact, achieving Net Zero goals, and developing digital solutions that protect the natural world.
These pillars form the foundation of our  Social Value Operating Model , which connects purpose to performance, ensuring our work aligns with national priorities, supports local communities, and delivers sustainable outcomes across our operations, partnerships, and client services.
During this period, the business was named among the Top 200 Women-Powered Businesses in the UK by JP Morgan, ranking as the number one full-service technology delivery and consultancy on the list . This recognition reflects our leadership diversity, inclusive culture, and commitment to equitable growth.
Our purpose continues to drive real-world outcomes, contributing to a healthier, safer, and cleaner world through digital innovation and collaboration. Highlights of the year include:
Environmental leadership:  Winning the  2025 AGI Environment and Sustainability Award  with  NatureScot  for our AI-enabled platform, InformedINSIGHT ™ , which supports Scotland’s 30-by-30 biodiversity targets.
Healthcare innovation:  Supporting the  Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)  to harness AI in accelerating the safe introduction of new treatments and medical devices – featured on  BBC Radio 4’s The Today Programme .
Clean energy and transport:  Supporting the transition to clean vehicles and energy infrastructure by providing advanced geospatial and data-driven insights that optimise renewable energy siting and operations in our work with Department for Transport and The Crown Estate.
Community wellbeing:  Delivering mental health training to 80 employees, raising over £6,000 for health charities, and deepening partnerships with  Manchester Mind  and  Prevent Breast Cancer .
Skills for growth:  Recruiting 18 new graduates and placement students, supporting 25% of staff to progress in their careers through promotions, and expanding our  Foundations of Delivery Learning Programme  to 30+ learning modules.
Responsible business practices:  Awarded the  UK Government Fair Payment Code Gold Award  and  Gold Standard for Prompt Payment , maintaining a  +70% local supplier base  and strong ethical governance.
Sustainability performance:  Publishing our refreshed  Carbon Reduction Plan (January 2025) , achieving 100% technology recycling and reuse, and embedding sustainable operations across all sites.
Each of these achievements demonstrates how Informed’ purpose, values, and business strategy translate into tangible benefits for its people, clients, and society at large.
THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
CHAIR'S STATEMENT AND STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2025
- 6 -
Prospects for 2025 - 2026
Informed has met its growth, development, and values commitments throughout each period for the past six years, demonstrating a responsible and effective approach to data science-led innovation, alongside the delivery of world-class, award-winning digital transformation services to a increased number of clients both in the UK and internationally.
100% client retention during the period, aligned with significant organic growth and new client wins across key growth markets in the last quarter, has strengthened Informed’s growth potential for the coming 12 months.
Informed’s Board has been ably supported by an increasingly mature senior leadership team, which has ensured sustainable progress, achievement, and commercial success through the period. Our people and partners have built an enviable, market-leading reputation for service delivery and product development, significantly growing our client base and diversifying into new markets.
Looking to the 2025-2026 period, the business will continue to deliver significant client work at scale. A strong pipeline of business has been built across private- and public-sector markets, both domestically and internationally.
In maintaining capability, capacity, and revenues over the 2024-2025 period, I would like to recognise the hard work, dedication, resilience, and support of our people and partners whose efforts have laid the foundations for significant growth in the next period.
I am encouraged by the sustained performance demonstrated through 2024-2025, and look forward with optimism to working with our growing domestic and international teams, our strengthened and upskilled partner network, and our extended client community to achieve further success over the next 12 months.
On behalf of the board
Dr J S Alderson
Chair, The Informed Group
19 December 2025

- 7 -
The directors present their annual report and financial statements for the year ended 30 September 2025.
Principal activities
The principal activity of the company and group continued to be that of the delivery of digital data and technology solutions.
Results and dividends
The results for the year are set out on page 12.
Ordinary dividends were paid amounting to £1,225,000. The directors do not recommend payment of a further dividend.
Directors
The directors who held office during the year and up to the date of signature of the financial statements were as follows:
Dr J S Alderson
Ms E T Vega
Future developments
Information about the future developments is provided in the strategic report.
Auditor
Cooper Parry Group Limited were appointed as auditor to the group and in accordance with section 485 of the Companies Act 2006, a resolution proposing that they be re-appointed will be put at a General Meeting.
Statement of directors' responsibilities
The directors are responsible for preparing the Annual Report and the financial statements in accordance with applicable law and regulations.
Company law requires the directors to prepare financial statements for each financial year. Under that law the directors have elected to prepare the financial statements in accordance with United Kingdom Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (United Kingdom Accounting Standards and applicable law). Under company law the directors must not approve the financial statements unless they are satisfied that they give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the group and company, and of the profit or loss of the group for that period. In preparing these financial statements, the directors are required to:
select suitable accounting policies and then apply them consistently;
make judgements and accounting estimates that are reasonable and prudent;
state whether applicable UK Accounting Standards have been followed, subject to any material departures disclosed and explained in the financial statements ;
prepare the financial statements on the going concern basis unless it is inappropriate to presume that the group and company will continue in business.
The directors are responsible for keeping adequate accounting records that are sufficient to show and explain the group’s and company’s transactions and disclose with reasonable accuracy at any time the financial position of the group and company and enable them to ensure that the financial statements comply with the Companies Act 2006. They are also responsible for safeguarding the assets of the group and company and hence for taking reasonable steps for the prevention and detection of fraud and other irregularities.
Statement of disclosure to auditor
So far as each person who was a director at the date of approving this report is aware, there is no relevant audit information of which the auditor of the company is unaware. Additionally, the directors individually have taken all the necessary steps that they ought to have taken as directors in order to make themselves aware of all relevant audit information and to establish that the auditor of the company is aware of that information.
THE INFORMED GROUP LIMITED
DIRECTORS' REPORT (CONTINUED)

Accounting policies
Company information
The Informed Group (“the company”) is a private limited company domiciled and incorporated in England and Wales . The registered office is The Old Bank. Old market Place, Altrincham, Cheshire, WA14 4PA
The group consists of The Informed Group Limited and all of its subsidiaries.
1.1
Basis of preparation
These financial statements have been prepared in accordance with FRS 102 “The Financial Reporting Standard applicable in the UK and Republic of Ireland” (“FRS 102”) and the requirements of the Companies Act 2006.
The financial statements are prepared in sterling , which is the functional currency of the company. Monetary a mounts in these financial statements are rounded to the nearest £.
The financial statements have been prepared under the historical cost convention. The principal accounting policies adopted are set out below.
The company is a qualifying entity for the purposes of FRS 102, being a member of a group where the parent of that group prepares publicly available consolidated financial statements, including this company, which are intended to give a true and fair view of the assets, liabilities, financial position and profit or loss of the group. The company has therefore taken advantage of exemptions from the following disclosure requirements for parent company information presented within the consolidated financial statements:
Section 7 ‘Statement of Cash Flows’: Presentation of a statement of cash flow and related notes and disclosures;
Section 11 ‘Basic Financial Instruments’ and Section 12 ‘Other Financial Instrument Issues : Interest income/expense and net gains/losses for financial instruments not measured at fair value; basis of determining fair values; details of collateral, loan defaults or breaches, details of hedges, hedging fair value changes recognised in profit or loss and in other comprehensive income;
Section 26 ‘Share based Payment’ : Share-based payment expense charged to profit or loss, reconciliation of opening and closing number and weighted average exercise price of share options, how the fair value of options granted was measured, measurement and carrying amount of liabilities for cash-settled share-based payments, explanation of modifications to arrangements ;
Section 33 ‘Related Party Disclosures’ : Compensation for key management personnel .
1.2
Business combinations
The consolidated financial statements presents the results of the Company and its own subsidiaries ("the Group") as if they form a single entity. Intercompany transactions and balance between group companies are therefore eliminated in full.
The consolidated financial statements incorporate the results of the business combinations using the merger accounting method.
1.3
Basis of consolidation
The consolidated group financial statements consist of the financial statements of the parent company The Informed Group Limited together with all entities controlled by the parent company (its subsidiaries) and the group’s share of its interests in joint ventures and associates .
All financial statements are made up to 30 September 2025 . Where necessary, adjustments are made to the financial statements of subsidiaries to bring the accounting policies used into line with those used by other members of the g roup.
U nrealised gains on transactions between group companies are eliminated on consolidation. Unrealised losses are also eliminated unless the transaction provides evidence of an impairment of the asset transferred.

1.4
Going concern
The Group's business activities, together with the factors likely to affect the future development, financial performance and financial position are set out in the Strategic report.
The group meets its day to day working capital requirements through its cash holdings and bank facilities.
The directors have prepared a going concern assessment based on board approved forecasts and strategic plans and these demonstrate the the group will have sufficient finance through a period of at least 12 months from the date of approval of these financial statements. The directors have also considered the covenants attached the borrowings and are satisfied that the covenant compliance will continue through the review period.
On the basis of the assessment, a t the time of approving the financial statements , t he directors have a reasonable expectation that the group has adequate resources to continue in operational existence for the foreseeable future. Thus t he directors continue to adopt the going concern basis of accounting in preparing the financial statements.
1.5
Turnover
Turnover is recognised at the fair value of the consideration received or receivable for goods and services provided in the normal course of business, and is shown net of VAT and other sales related taxes. The fair value of consideration takes into account trade discounts, settlement discounts and volume rebates.
When cash inflows are deferred and represent a financing arrangement, the fair value of the consideration is the present value of the future receipts. The difference between the fair value of the consideration and the nominal amount received is recognised as interest income.
Rendering of services
Revenue from a contract to provide services is recognised in the period in which the services are provided in accordance with the stage of completion of the contract when all of the following conditions are satisfied:
• the amount of revenue can be measured reliably;
• it is probable that the Company will receive the consideration due under the contract;
• the stage of completion of the contract at the end of the reporting period can be measured reliably; and
• the costs incurred and the costs to complete the contract can be measured reliably.
Revenue which has been recognised but not invoiced by the reporting date is included in debtors in ‘accrued income’. Amounts invoiced in advance are included in ‘accruals and deferred income’.
1.6
Intangible fixed assets other than goodwill
Intangible assets acquired separately from a business are recognised at cost and are subsequently measured at cost less accumulated amortisation and accumulated impairment losses.
Intangible assets acquired on business combinations are recognised separately from goodwill at the acquisition date where it is probable that the expected future economic benefits that are attributable to the asset will flow to the entity and the fair value of the asset can be measured reliably; the intangible asset arises from contractual or other legal rights; and the intangible asset is separable from the entity.
Amortisation is recognised so as to write off the cost of assets less their residual values over their useful lives on the following bases:

1.8
Fixed asset investments
Equity in vest ments are measured at fair value through profit or loss , except for those equity investments that are not publicly traded and whose fair value cannot otherwise be measured reliably , which are recognised at cost less impairment until a reliable measure of fair value becomes available.
I n the parent company financial statements, investments in subsidiaries are initially measured at cost and subsequently measured at cost less any accumulated impairment losses.
A subsidiary is an entity controlled by the group. Control is the power to govern the financial and operating policies of the entity so as to obtain benefits from its activities.
1.9
Impairment of fixed assets
At each reporting period end date, the group reviews the carrying amounts of its tangible and intangible assets to determine whether there is any indication that those assets have suffered an impairment loss. If any such indication exists, the recoverable amount of the asset is estimated in order to determine the extent of the impairment loss (if any). Where it is not possible to estimate the recoverable amount of an individual asset, the company estimates the recoverable amount of the cash-generating unit to which the asset belongs.
The carrying amount of the investments accounted for using the equity method is tested for impairment as a single asset. Any goodwill included in the carrying amount of the investment is not tested separately for impairment.
1.10
Cash and cash equivalents
Cash is represented by cash in hand and deposits with financial institutions repayable without penalty on notice of not more than 24 hour. C ash equivalents are short-term liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less . Bank overdrafts are shown within borrowings in current liabilities.

1.11
Financial instruments
The group has elected to apply the provisions of Section 11 ‘Basic Financial Instruments’ to all of its financial instruments.
Financial instruments are recognised in the group's balance sheet when the group becomes party to the contractual provisions of the instrument.
Financial assets and liabilities are offset and the net amounts presented in the financial statements when there is a legally enforceable right to set off the recognised amounts and there is an intention to settle on a net basis or to realise the asset and settle the liability simultaneously.
Basic financial assets
Basic financial assets, which include debtors and cash and bank balances, are initially measured at transaction price including transaction costs and are subsequently carried at amortised cost using the effective interest m ethod unless the arrangement constitutes a financing transaction, where the transaction is measured at the present value of the future receipts discounted at a market rate of interest. Financial assets classified as receivable within one year are not amortised.
Impairment of financial assets
Financial assets, other than those held at fair value through profit and loss , are assessed for indicators of impairment at each reporting end date.
Financial assets are impaired where there is objective evidence that, as a result of one or more events that occurred after the initial recognition of the financial asset, the estimated future cash flows have been affected. If an asset is impaired, the impairment loss is the difference between the carrying amount and the present value of the estimated cash flows discounted at the asset’s original effective interest rate. The impairment loss is recognised in profit or loss.
If there is a decrease in the impairment loss arising from an event occurring after the impairment was recognised, the impairment is reversed. The reversal is such that the current carrying amount does not exceed what the carrying amount would have been, had the impairment not previously been recognised. The impairment reversal is recognised in profit or loss.
Derecognition of financial assets
Financial assets are derecognised only when the contractual rights to the cash flows from the asset expire or are settled, or when the group transfers the financial asset and substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership to another entity, or if some significant risks and rewards of ownership are retained but control of the asset has transferred to another party that is able to sell the asset in its entirety to an unrelated third party.
Classification of financial liabilities
Financial liabilities and equity instruments are classified according to the substance of the contractual arrangements entered into. An equity instrument is any contract that evidences a residual interest in the assets of the group after deducting all of its liabilities.
Basic financial liabilities
Basic financial liabilities, including creditors , bank loans, loans from fellow group companies and preference shares that are classified as debt, are initially recognised at transaction price unless the arrangement constitutes a financing transaction, where the debt instrument is measured at the present value of the future paymen ts discounted at a market rate of interest. Financial liabilities classified as payable within one year are not amortised.
Debt instruments are subsequently carried at amortised cost, using the effective interest rate method.

Equity instruments issued by the group are recorded at the proceeds received, net of transaction costs. Dividends payable on equity instruments are recognised as liabilities once they are no longer at the discretion of the group.
1.13
Taxation
The tax expense represents the sum of the tax currently payable and deferred tax.
Current tax
The tax currently payable is based on taxable profit for the year. Taxable profit differs from net profit as reported in the profit and loss account because it excludes items of income or expense that are taxable or deductible in other years and it further excludes items that are never taxable or deductible. The group’s liability for current tax is calculated using tax rates that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the reporting end date.
Deferred tax
Deferred tax liabilities are generally recognised for all timing differences and deferred tax assets are recognised to the extent that it is probable that they will be recovered against the reversal of deferred tax liabilities or other future taxable profits. Such assets and liabilities are not recognised if the timing difference arises from goodwill or from the initial recognition of other assets and liabilities in a transaction that affects neither the tax profit nor the accounting profit.
The carrying amount of deferred tax assets is reviewed at each reporting end date and reduced to the extent that it is no longer probable that sufficient taxable profits will be available to allow all or part of the asset to be recovered. Deferred tax is calculated at the tax rates that are expected to apply in the period when the liability is settled or the asset is realised. Deferred tax is charged or credited in the profit and loss account , except when it relates to items charged or credited directly to equity, in which case the deferred tax is also dealt with in equity. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are offset if, and only if, there is a legally enforceable right to offset current tax assets and liabilities and the deferred tax assets and liabilities relate to taxes levied by the same tax authority.
1.14
Employee benefits
The costs of short-term employee benefits are recognised as a liability and an expense, unless those costs are required to be recognised as part of the cost of stock or fixed assets .
The cost of any unused holiday entitlement is recognised in the period in which the employee’s services are received.
Termination benefits are recognised immediately as an expense when the company is demonstrably committed to terminate the employment of an employee or to provide termination benefits.
1.15
Retirement benefits
Payments to defined contribution retirement benefit schemes are charged as an expense as they fall due.
1.16
Leases
Rentals payable under operating leases, including any lease incentives received, are charged to profit or loss on a straight line basis over the term of the relevant lease except where another more systematic basis is more representative of the time pattern in which economic benefits from the lease d asset are consumed.
